# Identify file locations and load libraries

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)

input_file <- "../data/raw/03-all_metrics_sample-level.csv"
run_label <- "pre_cleaning"

# AFTER cleaning, change ONLY these two settings:
# input_file <- "04-all_metrics_sample-level_CLEANED.csv"
# run_label <- "post_cleaning"

stopifnot(file.exists(input_file))
output_dir <- file.path("../output/raw_eda", run_label)
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Shared definitions for a fair pre/post comparison.
metric_names <- c("p450", "sod", "shell", "condition_index",
                  "weight_initial", "weight_final", "weight_change",
                  "length", "width", "height")
```

# Load combined measurements

```{r}
#| label: read-combined
raw_data <- read_csv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

required_columns <- c("sample_id", "site_number", "reporting_area", metric_names)
stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(raw_data)))

# Work on a new object; don't mutate the source CSV.
data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(sample_id = as.character(sample_id),
         site_number = as.character(site_number),
         reporting_area = as.character(reporting_area))

# A short handoff check, not a full audit of original files.
stopifnot(nrow(data) > 0)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(data$sample_id))
stopifnot(is.numeric(data$p450), is.numeric(data$sod),
          is.numeric(data$shell), is.numeric(data$condition_index),
          is.numeric(data$weight_initial), is.numeric(data$weight_final),
          is.numeric(data$weight_change), is.numeric(data$length),
          is.numeric(data$width), is.numeric(data$height))

nrow(data)
n_distinct(data$sample_id)
n_distinct(data$site_number)
glimpse(data)
```

# Review completeness and zero values

This is **measurement-level EDA**, not the prior multi-sheet reconciliation checklist. Report zeros and negatives; don't replace them here.

```{r}
#| label: long-and-missingness
long_data <- data %>%
  select(sample_id, site_number, reporting_area, all_of(metric_names)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(metric_names), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value")

missingness <- long_data %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  summarise(n_total = n(), n_observed = sum(!is.na(value)),
            n_missing = sum(is.na(value)), pct_missing = 100 * mean(is.na(value)),
            n_zero = sum(value == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_negative = sum(value < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_nonfinite = sum(!is.finite(value) & !is.na(value)),
            .groups = "drop")
missingness
```

# Univariate descriptive statistics

We include sample size, central tendency, spread (SD, IQR, MAD), coefficient of variation, and a *descriptive* t-based confidence interval. The t-based interval below assumes observations are independent; the mussels are clustered by site, so this is **not** the appropriate inferential CI for site or regional effects. CV can be misleading for signed variables or means near zero.

```{r}
#| label: descriptions
metric_summary <- long_data %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)),
            mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            variance = var(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            q1 = quantile(value, .25, na.rm = TRUE),
            q3 = quantile(value, .75, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            iqr = IQR(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            mad_scaled = mad(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(se = sd / sqrt(n),
         ci95_low = if_else(n > 1, mean - qt(.975, n - 1) * se, NA_real_),
         ci95_high = if_else(n > 1, mean + qt(.975, n - 1) * se, NA_real_),
         cv_pct = if_else(n > 1 & abs(mean) > 1e-8, 100 * sd / abs(mean), NA_real_))
metric_summary
```

# Visualize individual measurements

## Histograms, dot plots, and boxplots

```{r}
#| label: histograms
#| fig-height: 10
ggplot(long_data, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "Sample-level histograms", x = "Measurement (unit differs by panel)", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: observations
#| fig-height: 10
ggplot(long_data, aes(x = metric, y = value)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, size = 0.8, alpha = 0.4, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "Individual observations", x = NULL, y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

```{r}
#| label: boxplots
#| fig-height: 10
ggplot(long_data, aes(x = metric, y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.color = "firebrick", na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "Boxplots show potential extremes, not errors", x = NULL, y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

## Q–Q plots and normality

Normality of the **raw marginal measurements** is not a prerequisite for every analysis. For models, the residuals, design and independence assumptions matter more. Shapiro–Wilk p-values below are an optional illustration, not a test-selection switch. A p-value below 0.05 is evidence *against* normality; a p-value above 0.05 is **not** proof of normality.

```{r}
#| label: qq
#| fig-height: 10
ggplot(long_data, aes(sample = value)) +
  stat_qq(na.rm = TRUE) + stat_qq_line(na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "Sample-level Q–Q diagnostics") + theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: shapiro-example
# Illustrative tests for two named variables; review plots and sample structure.
# shapiro.test requires 3–5000 finite observations with some variation.
shapiro.test(data$p450[is.finite(data$p450)])
shapiro.test(data$sod[is.finite(data$sod)])
shapiro.test(data$condition_index[is.finite(data$condition_index)])
shapiro.test(data$shell[is.finite(data$shell)])
```

# 6. Outlier screens (retain every observation)

Use *three different descriptions of extreme observations*: Tukey's 1.5 × IQR fence, a conventional z-score, and a median/MAD-based robust score. Flags can disagree. They do not justify deletion by themselves. In the long table, the same sample can be flagged for different measurements; investigate the specific sample × metric combination.

```{r}
#| label: flags
flags <- long_data %>%
  left_join(metric_summary %>%
              select(metric, mean, median, sd, q1, q3, iqr, mad_scaled),
            by = "metric") %>%
  mutate(iqr_low = q1 - 1.5 * iqr,
         iqr_high = q3 + 1.5 * iqr,
         iqr_flag = !is.na(value) & (value < iqr_low | value > iqr_high),
         z_score = if_else(!is.na(sd) & sd > 0, (value - mean) / sd, NA_real_),
         z_flag = !is.na(z_score) & abs(z_score) > 3,
         robust_z = if_else(!is.na(mad_scaled) & mad_scaled > 0,
                            (value - median) / mad_scaled, NA_real_),
         robust_flag = !is.na(robust_z) & abs(robust_z) > 3.5,
         any_flag = iqr_flag | z_flag | robust_flag)

flag_counts <- flags %>%
  group_by(metric) %>%
  summarise(n_iqr = sum(iqr_flag), n_z = sum(z_flag),
            n_robust = sum(robust_flag), n_any = sum(any_flag),
            .groups = "drop")
flag_counts

flagged_observations <- flags %>%
  filter(any_flag) %>%
  select(sample_id, site_number, metric, value,
         iqr_low, iqr_high, z_score, robust_z,
         iqr_flag, z_flag, robust_flag) %>%
  arrange(metric, site_number, sample_id)
flagged_observations
```

**Discussion:** Do extremes cluster within a site? Could they reflect organism size, a local stressor, assay detection limits, transcription errors, or something else? Check methods and records before making decisions. Comparing all individual mussels against one pooled distribution may flag genuine *between-site* variation as extreme.

# 7. Site-level EDA: replication and summaries

Site is the primary grouping unit here; reporting area is a secondary spatial grouping. Use site **number** as the stable grouping key. Grouped means are descriptive and do not replace sample-level records.

```{r}
#| label: site-replication
site_replication <- data %>%
  group_by(site_number) %>%
  summarise(n_mussels = n(), .groups = "drop")
site_replication

ggplot(site_replication, aes(x = n_mussels)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Mussels sampled per site", x = "Number of mussels", y = "Number of sites") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: site-summary
site_summary <- long_data %>%
  group_by(site_number, reporting_area, metric) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(!is.na(value)),
            mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            mad_scaled = mad(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
site_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: within-site
#| fig-height: 8
long_data %>%
  filter(metric %in% c("p450", "sod", "shell", "condition_index")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(site_number), y = value)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.16, alpha = 0.5, size = 0.7, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Within-site distributions: selected metrics", x = "Site number", y = "Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, size = 5))
```

```{r}
#| label: ranked-sites
#| fig-height: 8
site_summary %>%
  filter(metric %in% c("p450", "sod", "shell", "condition_index")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(site_number, mean), y = mean)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) + coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "Site-level metric means (common site order across panels)", x = "Site", y = "Site mean") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 5))
```

# 8. Reporting-area exploration (secondary grouping)

Each reporting area contains multiple sites. The area-level summary below treats **site means** as its observations (not each mussel), to avoid giving extra statistical weight to sites with more mussels.

```{r}
#| label: area-summary
area_summary <- site_summary %>%
  group_by(reporting_area, metric) %>%
  summarise(n_sites = n(), mean_of_site_means = mean(mean, na.rm = TRUE),
            median_of_site_means = median(mean, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_between_sites = sd(mean, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
area_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: area-plot
#| fig-height: 9
site_summary %>%
  filter(metric %in% c("p450", "sod", "shell", "condition_index")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(reporting_area), y = mean)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, na.rm = TRUE) +
  geom_jitter(width = .15, alpha = .7, size = 1, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "Between-site variation within reporting areas", x = "Reporting area", y = "Site mean") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 9. Bivariate and multivariate exploration

Use sample-level scatterplots to inspect organism-level relationships, and site means for an exploratory cross-site matrix. Correlations are not causal evidence; their interpretation changes with the unit of analysis. PCA, PERMANOVA and post-hoc significance testing are **deferred to the later analysis module**, after cleaning choices and a research question are established.

```{r}
#| label: scatterplots
ggplot(data, aes(x = length, y = shell)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Sample-level shell length vs thickness", x = "Length", y = "Shell thickness") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(data, aes(x = p450, y = sod)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.55) +
  labs(title = "Sample-level biomarker comparison", x = "P450", y = "SOD") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: site-matrix
site_wide <- site_summary %>%
  select(site_number, metric, mean) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = mean)

# Choose interpretable, nonredundant measurements for a readable matrix.
site_pairs <- site_wide %>%
  select(p450, sod, shell, length, condition_index)

pairs(site_pairs, main = "Site-mean scatterplot matrix", pch = 19, cex = 0.5)
cor(site_pairs, method = "pearson", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
cor(site_pairs, method = "spearman", use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
```

# 10. Optional transformation *diagnostics* (do not replace raw values)

Examine whether a transformation may make a distribution more interpretable, without quietly making it permanent. **Log transforms require strictly positive values.** The original SOD data may contain nonpositive observations; leave those as missing **in this diagnostic column only**. Whether a nonpositive value is a meaningful observation, below LOD, or an artifact is decided separately. A log1p transform is not a neutral substitute for analytical rules.

```{r}
#| label: transformations
transform_preview <- data %>%
  mutate(p450_log10_preview = if_else(p450 > 0, log10(p450), NA_real_),
         sod_log10_preview = if_else(sod > 0, log10(sod), NA_real_))

#| fig-height: 7
transform_preview %>%
  select(p450, p450_log10_preview, sod, sod_log10_preview) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, fill = "steelblue", color = "white", na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Raw versus log10 diagnostic distributions", x = "Value") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# 11. Export outputs for comparison and decisions

The EDA **does not write a cleaned dataset**. It exports diagnostics, selected site-level summaries, and a copy of the input data labeled with this run. After a separate cleaning script creates a cleaned CSV, rerun this document under `post_cleaning`. Keep both report outputs and compare counts, distributions and site-level patterns before moving to inference.

```{r}
#| label: export
write_csv(data, file.path(output_dir, "00_input_snapshot_UNMODIFIED.csv"))
write_csv(missingness, file.path(output_dir, "01_missingness.csv"))
write_csv(metric_summary, file.path(output_dir, "02_metric_descriptives.csv"))
write_csv(flag_counts, file.path(output_dir, "03_outlier_flag_counts.csv"))
write_csv(flagged_observations, file.path(output_dir, "04_flagged_observations_REVIEW.csv"))
write_csv(site_replication, file.path(output_dir, "05_site_replication.csv"))
write_csv(site_summary, file.path(output_dir, "06_site_metric_summary.csv"))
write_csv(area_summary, file.path(output_dir, "07_area_metric_summary.csv"))
```

# 12. Student interpretation and decisions to carry forward

Answer in the lab notebook before any cleaning actions:

1. Which metrics are skewed or multimodal? Are patterns shared across sites?
2. Are zeros and negative values expected by the assay and biological sign conventions?
3. Which observations are flagged by IQR but not MAD (or vice versa)? What original records would you check?
4. What differences emerge between the sample-level and site-level pictures?
5. Would any transformation help a *specific downstream model*, or merely change the appearance of the plot?
6. Which candidate cleaning rule could change site rankings, site-level variance, or the number of complete-case observations?
7. What would count as evidence that cleaning was beneficial rather than simply making a figure look tidier?

**Documentation standard:** log sample ID, metric, original value, reason for review, evidence checked, proposed treatment, who approved the decision, and the resulting value; include excluded records in the log. Keep **an unchanged raw CSV** and a **new cleaned CSV** with a version/date. For pre/post comparisons, hold the definitions and visual choices constant.

## Comparison checklist after post-cleaning EDA

Compare the pre/post `01_missingness.csv`, `02_metric_descriptives.csv`, `03_outlier_flag_counts.csv`, `05_site_replication.csv`, and `06_site_metric_summary.csv`. A change in sample size may be appropriate, but must be explained. Do not read a higher Shapiro p-value or fewer flagged records as independent evidence that cleaning was correct.
